items.s: Don't be ___ to your little sister. Be nice!
items.tip: un- means 'not': kind → unkind (not kind).
items.say: Don't be unkind to your little sister. Be nice!
items.ask: Don't be blank to your little sister. Be nice!

items.s: I ___ with you. I think cats are better than dogs.
items.tip: dis- makes the opposite of some verbs: agree → disagree.
items.say: I disagree with you. I think cats are better than dogs.
items.ask: I blank with you. I think cats are better than dogs.

items.s: It's ___ to finish this puzzle in one minute!
items.tip: Many words starting with p take im- for 'not': possible → impossible.
items.say: It's impossible to finish this puzzle in one minute!
items.ask: It's blank to finish this puzzle in one minute!

items.s: Your room is very ___. Please tidy it!
items.tip: un- + tidy = untidy (not tidy).
items.say: Your room is very untidy. Please tidy it!
items.ask: Your room is very blank. Please tidy it!

items.s: The magician made the rabbit ___.
items.tip: dis- + appear = disappear (the opposite of appear).
items.say: The magician made the rabbit disappear.
items.ask: The magician made the rabbit blank.

items.s: It's ___ to talk with your mouth full.
items.tip: polite starts with p, so 'not polite' is impolite.
items.say: It's impolite to talk with your mouth full.
items.ask: It's blank to talk with your mouth full.

items.s: The cat looked very ___ when it got wet.
items.tip: un- + happy = unhappy (not happy). The sentence tells us the cat was sad.
items.say: The cat looked very unhappy when it got wet.
items.ask: The cat looked very blank when it got wet.

items.s: My brother ___ broccoli. He never eats it.
items.tip: dis- + like = dislike, and with he/she we add -s: he dislikes.
items.say: My brother dislikes broccoli. He never eats it.
items.ask: My brother blank broccoli. He never eats it.

items.s: Thank you for your ___!
items.tip: After your we need a noun (a thing word): kind + -ness = kindness.
items.say: Thank you for your kindness!
items.ask: Thank you for your blank!

items.s: There was a lot of ___ before the school play.
items.tip: a lot of + noun: excite + -ment = excitement.
items.say: There was a lot of excitement before the school play.
items.ask: There was a lot of blank before the school play.

items.s: We got an ___ to Emma's birthday party.
items.tip: an + noun: invite → invitation (drop the e, add -ation).
items.say: We got an invitation to Emma's birthday party.
items.ask: We got an blank to Emma's birthday party.

items.s: I'm scared of the ___, so I sleep with a night light.
items.tip: the + noun: dark + -ness = darkness.
items.say: I'm scared of the darkness, so I sleep with a night light.
items.ask: I'm scared of the blank, so I sleep with a night light.

items.s: The dancers practised every ___ of the dance.
items.tip: every + noun: move + -ment = movement.
items.say: The dancers practised every movement of the dance.
items.ask: The dancers practised every blank of the dance.

items.s: Can you give me some ___ about the school trip?
items.tip: some + noun: inform + -ation = information.
items.say: Can you give me some information about the school trip?
items.ask: Can you give me some blank about the school trip?

items.s: Mum made a big ___: we can have a puppy!
items.tip: a + noun: decide → decision (the d changes to s).
items.say: Mum made a big decision: we can have a puppy!
items.ask: Mum made a big blank: we can have a puppy!

items.s: The children shouted with ___ when they won.
items.tip: with + noun: happy + -ness, and y changes to i: happiness.
items.say: The children shouted with happiness when they won.
items.ask: The children shouted with blank when they won.

items.s: This new sofa is very ___.
items.tip: very + adjective: comfort + -able = comfortable.
items.say: This new sofa is very comfortable.
items.ask: This new sofa is very blank.

items.s: Don't be so ___! You dropped your lunch again.
items.tip: -less means 'without': careless = without care.
items.say: Don't be so careless! You dropped your lunch again.
items.ask: Don't be so blank! You dropped your lunch again.

items.s: Climbing on the roof is ___.
items.tip: -ous makes an adjective: danger → dangerous.
items.say: Climbing on the roof is dangerous.
items.ask: Climbing on the roof is blank.

items.s: She wants to be a ___ singer one day.
items.tip: fame + -ous: drop the e: famous.
items.say: She wants to be a famous singer one day.
items.ask: She wants to be a blank singer one day.

items.s: We had a very ___ day at the water park.
items.tip: -able = can be enjoyed: enjoy + -able = enjoyable.
items.say: We had a very enjoyable day at the water park.
items.ask: We had a very blank day at the water park.

items.s: It was so ___ that we couldn't see the hills.
items.tip: Weather + -y. fog has one vowel + one consonant, so double the g: foggy.
items.say: It was so foggy that we couldn't see the hills.
items.ask: It was so blank that we couldn't see the hills.

items.s: This old torch is ___ now. It doesn't work.
items.tip: -less = without: useless = no use at all.
items.say: This old torch is useless now. It doesn't work.
items.ask: This old torch is blank now. It doesn't work.

items.s: The paths were ___ this morning, so we walked slowly.
items.tip: ice + -y: drop the e: icy.
items.say: The paths were icy this morning, so we walked slowly.
items.ask: The paths were blank this morning, so we walked slowly.
